docs.title: CHAMOIS
docs.text:
CHAMOIS is a mini control stack for a simulated trapped-ion quantum computer. It follows the path a circuit takes on a real machine, from the user-facing API down to timed laser pulses:

  1. An ARNICA-style job API accepts circuits in AQT's native gates (R, RZ, RXX, MEASURE) and moves jobs through queued → ongoing → finished / error / cancelled.
  2. A Rust scheduler (PyO3 bindings) compiles the gates into a nanosecond-timed pulse timeline per laser channel, using per-ion calibration data, and rejects overlaps and timing violations, following the RTIO model of ARTIQ.
  3. A simulated 10-ion device runs the timeline on a statevector. It only sees pulses, so the rotation angles come from pulse durations and calibrated π times, as on hardware.
  4. Results for Bell and GHZ circuits are cross-checked against Qiskit's statevector and against the offline simulator of AQT's qiskit-aqt-provider.

Not real hardware

CHAMOIS is a learning and demonstration project. The device is simulated, the calibration numbers are realistic for a 40Ca+ optical-qubit trap but invented, and there is no noise model yet.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The interactive OpenAPI page is served by the API itself at /docs. All routes except /health and the console need Authorization: Bearer <token>.

docs.title: ARNICA-compatible job API
docs.text:
Method Path Notes GET /api/v1/workspaces one workspace default with resource chamois GET /api/v1/resources/chamois available_qubits = enabled ions POST /api/v1/submit/{workspace}/{resource} body {job_type, label, payload: {circuits}} → queued GET /api/v1/result/{job_id} ?include_timing_data=true adds status timestamps DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} queued: dropped; ongoing: stops after the current circuit; 208 if already final

Job states: queued, ongoing (with finished_count), finished (with result), error (with message), cancelled.

docs.title: CHAMOIS extensions
docs.text: Method Path Role Notes GET /api/v1/me any who am I GET /api/v1/jobs any researchers see their own jobs, operators all GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/schedule?circuit=0 any compiled timeline + violations POST /api/v1/schedule any compile one circuit without running it GET /api/v1/calibration any current calibration PUT /api/v1/calibration operator new calibration version GET /api/v1/crosscheck any Bell/GHZ vs AQT offline simulator (cached per calibration) GET /health public version, scheduler backend, queue size

docs.title: Direct-access API (for qiskit-aqt-provider)
docs.text:
Method Path Notes GET /direct/status/ions {"num_ions": 10} GET /direct/system/name "chamois" PUT /direct/circuit one ARNICA circuit → job id GET /direct/circuit/result/{job_id} long poll until the job is final

Direct-access jobs go through the same queue and show up in the console with a qiskit tag.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Researcher
    participant API as FastAPI
    participant Q as Job worker
    participant S as Rust scheduler
    participant D as Simulated device
    U->>API: POST /api/v1/submit/default/chamois
    API-->>U: job_id, status "queued"
    Q->>Q: status "ongoing"
    loop each circuit
        Q->>S: compile(gates, calibration snapshot)
        S-->>Q: timeline + violations

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
JSON across the PyO3 boundary. The Rust function takes one JSON string and returns one. Pydantic validates on the Python side, serde on the Rust side. The boundary is easy to log and replay, and the Rust core has no PyO3 types, so cargo test and Clippy run without Python. PyO3 is an optional Cargo feature that maturin turns on. The GIL is released while Rust compiles.

A Python reference model. The same rules exist twice on purpose: Hypothesis generates thousands of random circuits and checks that Rust and Python produce identical timelines. It is the "golden model" technique used in hardware verification. It also lets the API run on a laptop without a Rust toolchain; production and CI set CHAMOIS_REQUIRE_RUST=1 so that fallback can never happen silently there.

The device sees pulses, not gates. Simulating the gates directly would make the scheduler invisible to the tests. Simulating the pulses means a wrong duration or phase changes the measured result.

One worker, one device. A QPU executes one circuit at a time, so a single asyncio worker drives it. Simulation runs in a thread (asyncio.to_thread) so the API stays responsive.

ARNICA compatibility. Matching AQT's public routes, field names, angle units and status values means existing clients work, and the API documents itself in the language AQT users already know.

docs.title: Run locally without Docker
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[qiskit,plot,dev]"      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\pip
.venv/bin/pip install ./scheduler                   # optional: needs a Rust toolchain
.venv/bin/chamois serve                             # http://127.0.0.1:8000

Without the Rust build, the API uses the Python reference scheduler and /health says "scheduler": "python".

The image builds the Rust wheel in a first stage and ships only the wheel, so the runtime image has no compiler.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text: Operators see the whole queue, cancel any job and edit the device calibration. In the demo, use the token operator-demo-token.

docs.title: Operator CLI
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[plot]"          # the CLI ships with the package
export CHAMOIS_URL=https://chamois-api.onrender.com
export CHAMOIS_TOKEN=operator-demo-token

chamois queue                      # all jobs, newest first
chamois calibration                # current calibration and version
chamois calibration --qubit 3 --pi-time 15100   # new pi time for ion 3, in ns
chamois calibration --disable 7    # stop addressing ion 7 (e.g. ion lost)
chamois calibration --enable 7
chamois timeline 3f2a91c0 --png timeline.png    # pulse timeline of a job (short id is fine)
chamois submit examples/ghz5.json --wait
chamois crosscheck                 # Bell/GHZ vs AQT offline simulator, runs locally

chamois timeline prints an ASCII plot (one row per channel) and, with --png, saves a matplotlib chart:

gate window 1001.0 - 1225.6 us (one shot: 2726.6 us)
     cool |c                                                                       |
  addr_q0 |#####===============================================================### |
  addr_q1 |     ===============================================================####|
 ms_drive |     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~   |
   detect |                                                                       d|
legend: # R pulse   = MS leg   ~ MS drive   c cooling   d detection

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Field Meaning Default qubits[i].pi_time_ns π rotation time of the addressed 729 nm beam on ion i 14.8–15.3 µs qubits[i].enabled disabled ions are never addressed true ms_gate_ns duration of a fully entangling MS gate, RXX(0.5) 200 µs cooling_ns Doppler + sideband cooling at the start of each shot 1000 µs detection_ns state detection at the end of each shot 1500 µs settle_ns minimum gap between two pulses on one channel (AOM switching) 1 µs clock_ns RTIO coarse clock: every timestamp is a multiple of it 8 ns max_sequence_ns coherence budget: one shot must finish within it 10 ms

Every save creates a new version (version, updated_by, updated_at). A job uses one calibration snapshot from start to end, and the job summary records which version it ran with.

docs.title: What can go wrong
docs.text: Message Cause What to do coherence_budget the shot is longer than max_sequence_ns shorten the circuit, or check the budget qubit_disabled a gate addresses a disabled ion re-enable the ion or remap the circuit qubit_out_of_range / too_many_qubits the circuit does not fit the register fix number_of_qubits overlap, settle_time, off_grid the timeline breaks the RTIO rules scheduler bug: the validator stopped it before the device ran

docs.title: Health and deployment
docs.text:
• GET /health returns the version, the scheduler backend (rust in production) and the queue size.
  • The Docker image sets CHAMOIS_REQUIRE_RUST=1, so the server refuses to start without the Rust build.
  • Jobs live in memory: a restart clears the queue (see Known limitations in the README).

docs.title: For researchers
docs.text: You can reach CHAMOIS in three ways: the web console, the ARNICA-style REST API, or Qiskit.

docs.title: 1. Qiskit, through AQT's own provider
docs.text:
CHAMOIS implements the small direct-access API that qiskit-aqt-provider uses for on-premise devices, so standard Qiskit circuits run unchanged through AQT's official client code:

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, transpile
from chamois.qiskit_bridge import chamois_backend

backend = chamois_backend("https://chamois-api.onrender.com", "researcher-demo-token")

bell = QuantumCircuit(2)
bell.h(0)
bell.cx(0, 1)
bell.measure_all()

native = transpile(bell, backend, optimization_level=3)  # -> R, RZ, RXX
print(backend.run(native, shots=200).result().get_counts())  # {'00': ~100, '11': ~100}

chamois_backend() is a one-liner around AQTProvider().direct_access().get_resource(url + "/direct", token). The full script is in examples/qiskit_on_chamois.py.

docs.title: 2. ARNICA-style REST API
docs.text:
The routes, field names and limits follow AQT's public ARNICA API (v1). Angles are in units of π.

TOKEN=researcher-demo-token
URL=https://chamois-api.onrender.com

curl -s -X POST "$URL/api/v1/submit/default/chamois" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @examples/bell.json
# {"job": {"job_id": "…", "resource_id": "chamois", …}, "response": {"status": "queued"}}

curl -s "$URL/api/v1/result/<job_id>?include_timing_data=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
Gate Fields Range R qubit, theta, phi θ ∈ [0, 1], φ ∈ [0, 2] RZ qubit, phi any finite φ (virtual, no pulse) RXX qubits (two different), theta θ ∈ [0, 0.5]; 0.5 is maximally entangling MEASURE — exactly once, last; measures all qubits

Limits: up to 50 circuits per job, 2000 shots and 2000 operations per circuit, 10 qubits on this device.

A finished job returns one list of shots per circuit; each shot is [bit of qubit 0, bit of qubit 1, …]:

{"status": "finished", "result": {"0": [[0, 0], [1, 1], [1, 1], [0, 0]]}}

If the scheduler rejects a circuit (for example a sequence longer than the coherence budget), the job ends in error with a readable message, and GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/schedule shows the timeline and the violations.

docs.title: 3. Web console
docs.text: Open the live demo, log in as Researcher, pick a preset and press Submit job. Click the job to see its pulse timeline per laser channel and the measured outcomes. Preview pulse schedule compiles a circuit without running it.

docs.title: Timing model: from gates to pulses
Channels
docs.text: Channel Physical meaning Used by cool global 397 nm beam for Doppler and sideband cooling start of every shot addr_q0 … addr_q9 addressed 729 nm beam on one ion R, and one leg of every RXX ms_drive bichromatic RF tone for Mølmer–Sørensen gates, shared by all ions RXX detect global 397 nm detection beam + camera/PMT end of every shot

docs.title: Rules (one shot)
docs.text:
1. Cooling first, from t = 0.
  2. Gates start after cooling plus the settle time. Each channel keeps its own cursor (the time it is free again), like the now cursor of ARTIQ's RTIO system. An operation starts as soon as all channels it needs are free, so gates on different ions run in parallel and gates on the same ion queue up.
  3. R(θ, φ) on ion q: duration = θ × π-time(q), phase = φ minus the ion's virtual-Z frame.
  4. RZ(φ) is virtual: no pulse, zero time. It adds φ to the ion's phase frame, and every later pulse on that ion is shifted by it. This is how trapped-ion systems usually implement Z rotations.
  5. RXX(θ) on ions a, b: duration = (θ / 0.5) × MS gate time, on addr_qa, addr_qb and ms_drive at once. Because ms_drive is shared, MS gates never overlap.
  6. Detection starts when every channel is free.
  7. Every timestamp and duration is rounded to the 8 ns RTIO clock (halves round up).
gantt
    title Bell pair: one shot (not to scale)
    dateFormat x
    axisFormat %L
    section cool
    cooling          :0, 1000
    section addr_q0
    R(1, 0)          :1001, 1016
    MS leg           :1017, 1217
    R(0.5, 1-frame)  :1218, 1226
    section addr_q1
    MS leg           :1017, 1217
    R(0.5, 1)        :1218, 1226
    section ms_drive
    MS drive         :1017, 1217
    section detect
    detection        :1227, 2727

docs.title: Validation (defence in depth)
docs.text:
After compiling, an independent validator checks the timeline before the device runs it. ARTIQ raises RTIOSequenceError when an event goes back in time on a channel; CHAMOIS rejects the equivalent problems up front:

Code Rule overlap two pulses on one channel overlap settle_time the gap between two pulses on one channel is shorter than settle_ns off_grid a timestamp or duration is not a multiple of the RTIO clock empty_pulse zero-length pulse qubit_disabled a pulse addresses a disabled ion coherence_budget the shot ends after max_sequence_ns

The compiler cannot produce the first four by construction. Hypothesis tests check exactly that on random circuits, and also break valid timelines on purpose to check the validator notices.

docs.title: How the device turns pulses back into physics
docs.text:
The simulated device reads only pulses: rotation angle = duration ÷ π-time, MS angle = 0.5 × duration ÷ MS gate time, axis = pulse phase. For two-qubit gates it applies exp(−i θπ/2 · σφa ⊗ σφb), with σφ = cos(φπ) X + sin(φπ) Y. Because RZ is virtual, the leftover frame at the end is a Z rotation, which does not change measurement results.

A wrong duration or phase in the scheduler would therefore show up as a wrong result. Hypothesis compares the pulse-level simulation with Qiskit's statevector on random native circuits (with a 1 ns clock the difference is below 10⁻³ TVD).
